evaluation_dimensions.name: Architecture
evaluation_dimensions.description: Core system design (micro‑services vs monolith), deployment models (cloud‑native, on‑prem, hybrid), and extensibility points. Highlights differences in container orchestration, API layers, and security zones. [doc_001]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Enterprise Latency / Throughput
evaluation_dimensions.description: Measured end‑to‑end processing latency and maximum concurrent inspection rates for both startup and enterprise tiers. Includes benchmark methodology and variance under peak load. [doc_002]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Pricing Predictability
evaluation_dimensions.description: Structure of subscription fees, usage‑based charges, and any hidden costs (e.g., over‑age inspection fees, support tiers). Evaluates clarity of pricing tiers and availability of volume discounts. [doc_003]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Advertised vs. Actual SLA
evaluation_dimensions.description: Comparison of vendor‑published service‑level agreements (uptime, response time, data retention) against third‑party monitoring data and customer‑reported incidents. [doc_004]

evaluation_dimensions.name: On-Prem / Hybrid Readiness
evaluation_dimensions.description: Support for Docker‑based deployment, Kubernetes integration, and requirements for on‑prem installations (hardware, licensing, support). Assesses ease of moving workloads between cloud and private environments. [doc_005]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Customer Sentiment & Trust
evaluation_dimensions.description: Aggregated sentiment from reviews, NPS scores, analyst ratings, and case‑study references. Captures perceived reliability, support quality, and roadmap confidence. [doc_006]

quotes.quote: CloudScale reduced our Groq and OpenAI token costs by 28% within the first month. However, documentation for custom Python middleware is sparse, and we experienced two 3-hour outages in Q2 where support disputed our 10x SLA credit claim citing upstream cloud network degradations.

The semantic cache hit rate hovers around 22% in production, which is lower than the advertised 40%. The UI dashboard is intuitive, but on-prem installation took four weeks instead of the promised 48 hours.

DataPulse is unrivaled for real-time latency. Our fleet routing agents query fresh sensor states in 6ms. Be careful with high-volume Kafka topics, however; overage fees doubled our invoice in month three before we configured filtering.
Reduced our MTTR from 45 minutes to 11 minutes for recurring database and pod connection incidents. The safety guardrails are solid—it has never accidentally executed an unsafe command in production.

Veloce caught three sophisticated indirect prompt injection attempts during our clinical pilot. The false positive rate on medical abbreviations is slightly annoying (around 4%), but their customer support helped tune custom bypass dictionaries quickly.

outages_and_incidents.description: Two separate three‑hour service outages occurred in Q2; the vendor’s support team contested the customer’s request for a 10× SLA credit, attributing the failures to upstream cloud network degradation.

praise_and_positive_outcomes.description: Achieved a 28% reduction in Groq and OpenAI token costs within the first month of deployment.
Delivered sub‑10 ms real‑time latency for fleet routing queries, highlighting strong performance for high‑frequency sensor data.
Cut mean time to recovery (MTTR) from 45 minutes to 11 minutes for recurring database and pod connection incidents; safety guardrails prevented unsafe command execution in production.
Successfully detected three sophisticated indirect prompt‑injection attempts during a clinical pilot, demonstrating effective security controls.
User interface dashboard described as intuitive, facilitating easier monitoring and management.

usability_and_friction_points.description: Documentation for building custom Python middleware is described as sparse, creating integration friction.
Observed semantic cache hit rate of 22 %—significantly below the advertised 40 %—and on‑premise installation took four weeks versus the promised 48 hours.
High‑volume Kafka topics triggered overage fees that doubled the invoice in month three until proper filtering was applied.
False‑positive rate on medical abbreviations is around 4 %, causing minor annoyance for end users.
